33:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
33:1.en: O Prophet! Keep thy duty to Allah and obey not the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Lo! Allah is Knower, Wise

33:2.ar: وَٱتَّبِعۡ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
33:2.en: And follow that which is inspired in thee from thy Lord. Lo! Allah is Aware of what ye do

33:3.ar: وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلࣰ ا
33:3.en: And put thy trust in Allah, for Allah is sufficient as Trustee

33:4.ar: مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلࣲ مِّن قَلۡبَيۡنِ فِي جَوۡفِهِۦۚ وَمَا جَعَلَ أَزۡوَٰجَكُمُ ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي تُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنۡهُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۚ وَمَا جَعَلَ أَدۡعِيَآءَكُمۡ أَبۡنَآءَكُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ قَوۡلُكُم بِأَفۡوَٰهِكُمۡۖ وَٱللَّهُ يَقُولُ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَهُوَ يَهۡدِي ٱلسَّبِيلَ
33:4.en: Allah hath not assigned unto any man two hearts within his body, nor hath He made your wives whom ye declare (to be your mothers) your mothers, nor hath He made those whom ye claim (to be your sons) your sons. This is but a saying of your mouths. But Allah saith the truth and He showeth the way

33:5.ar: ٱدۡعُوهُمۡ لِأٓبَآئِهِمۡ هُوَ أَقۡسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَعۡلَمُوٓاْ ءَابَآءَهُمۡ فَإِخۡوَٰنُكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَمَوَٰلِيكُمۡۚ وَلَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحࣱ فِيمَآ أَخۡطَأۡتُم بِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتۡ قُلُوبُكُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمًا
33:5.en: Proclaim their real parentage. That will be more equitable in the sight of Allah. And if ye know not their fathers, then (they are) your brethren in the faith, and your clients. And there is no sin for you in the mistakes that ye make unintentionally, but what your hearts purpose (that will be a sin for you). Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

33:6.ar: ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَوۡلَىٰ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ مِنۡ أَنفُسِهِمۡۖ وَأَزۡوَٰجُهُۥٓ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡۗ وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ بَعۡضُهُمۡ أَوۡلَىٰ بِبَعۡضࣲ فِي كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ إِلَّآ أَن تَفۡعَلُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَوۡلِيَآئِكُم مَّعۡرُوفࣰ اۚ كَانَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مَسۡطُورࣰ ا
33:6.en: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their selves, and his wives are (as) their mothers. And the owners of kinship are closer one to another in the ordinance of Allah than (other) believers and the fugitives (who fled from Mecca), except that ye should do kindness to your friends. This is written in the Book (of nature)

33:7.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مِيثَٰقَهُمۡ وَمِنكَ وَمِن نُّوحࣲ وَإِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَۖ وَأَخَذۡنَا مِنۡهُم مِّيثَٰقًا غَلِيظࣰ ا
33:7.en: And when We exacted a covenant from the prophets, and from thee (O Muhammad) and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus son of Mary. We took from them a solemn covenant

33:8.ar: لِّيَسۡـَٔلَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ عَن صِدۡقِهِمۡۚ وَأَعَدَّ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
33:8.en: That He may ask the loyal of their loyalty. And He hath prepared a painful doom for the unfaithful

33:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذۡ جَآءَتۡكُمۡ جُنُودࣱ فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِيحࣰ ا وَجُنُودࣰ ا لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَاۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرًا
33:9.en: O ye who believe! Remember Allah's favour unto you when there came against you hosts, and We sent against them a great wind and hosts ye could not see. And Allah is ever Seer of what ye do

33:10.ar: إِذۡ جَآءُوكُم مِّن فَوۡقِكُمۡ وَمِنۡ أَسۡفَلَ مِنكُمۡ وَإِذۡ زَاغَتِ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلۡحَنَاجِرَ وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَا۠
33:10.en: When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when eyes grew wild and hearts reached to the throats, and ye were imagining vain thoughts concerning Allah

33:11.ar: هُنَالِكَ ٱبۡتُلِيَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَزُلۡزِلُواْ زِلۡزَالࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ ا
33:11.en: There were the believers sorely tried, and shaken with a mighty shock

33:12.ar: وَإِذۡ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ إِلَّا غُرُورࣰ ا
33:12.en: And when the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, were saying: Allah and His messenger promised us naught but delusion

33:13.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَت طَّآئِفَةࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَٰٓأَهۡلَ يَثۡرِبَ لَا مُقَامَ لَكُمۡ فَٱرۡجِعُواْۚ وَيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُ فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلنَّبِيَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنَا عَوۡرَةࣱ وَمَا هِيَ بِعَوۡرَةٍۖ إِن يُرِيدُونَ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
33:13.en: And when a party of them said: O folk of Yathrib! There is no stand (possible) for you, therefor turn back. And certain of them (even) sought permission of the Prophet, saying: Our homes lie open (to the enemy). And they lay not open. They but wished to flee

33:21.ar: لَّقَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ فِي رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةࣱ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلۡيَوۡمَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَ وَذَكَرَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا
33:21.en: Verily in the messenger of Allah ye have a good example for him who looketh unto Allah and the Last Day, and remembereth Allah much

33:22.ar: وَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابَ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥۚ وَمَا زَادَهُمۡ إِلَّآ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَتَسۡلِيمࣰ ا
33:22.en: And when the true believers saw the clans, they said: This is that which Allah and His messenger promised us. Allah and His messenger are true. It did but confirm them in their faith and resignation

33:28.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيۡنَ أُمَتِّعۡكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحۡكُنَّ سَرَاحࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
33:28.en: O Prophet! Say unto thy wives: If ye desire the world's life and its adornment, come! I will content you and will release you with a fair release

33:29.ar: وَإِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلۡمُحۡسِنَٰتِ مِنكُنَّ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
33:29.en: But if ye desire Allah and His messenger and the abode of the Hereafter, then lo! Allah hath prepared for the good among you an immense reward

33:30.ar: يَٰنِسَآءَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ مَن يَأۡتِ مِنكُنَّ بِفَٰحِشَةࣲ مُّبَيِّنَةࣲ يُضَٰعَفۡ لَهَا ٱلۡعَذَابُ ضِعۡفَيۡنِۚ وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرࣰ ا
33:30.en: O ye wives of the Prophet! Whosoever of you committeth manifest lewdness, the punishment for her will be doubled, and that is easy for Allah

33:31.ar: ۞وَمَن يَقۡنُتۡ مِنكُنَّ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحࣰ ا نُّؤۡتِهَآ أَجۡرَهَا مَرَّتَيۡنِ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهَا رِزۡقࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
33:31.en: And whosoever of you is submissive unto Allah and His messenger and doeth right, We shall give her her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a rich provision

33:32.ar: يَٰنِسَآءَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ لَسۡتُنَّ كَأَحَدࣲ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِنِ ٱتَّقَيۡتُنَّۚ فَلَا تَخۡضَعۡنَ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ فَيَطۡمَعَ ٱلَّذِي فِي قَلۡبِهِۦ مَرَضࣱ وَقُلۡنَ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّعۡرُوفࣰ ا
33:32.en: O ye wives of the Prophet! Ye are not like any other women. If ye keep your duty (to Allah), then be not soft of speech, lest he in whose heart is a disease aspire (to you), but utter customary speech

33:33.ar: وَقَرۡنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ وَأَقِمۡنَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتِينَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِعۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمُ ٱلرِّجۡسَ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمۡ تَطۡهِيرࣰ ا
33:33.en: And stay in your houses. Bedizen not yourselves with the bedizenment of the Time of Ignorance. Be regular in prayer, and pay the poor-due, and obey Allah and His messenger. Allah's wish is but to remove uncleanness far from you, O Folk of the Household, and cleanse you with a thorough cleansing

33:34.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡنَ مَا يُتۡلَىٰ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ لَطِيفًا خَبِيرًا
33:34.en: And bear in mind that which is recited in your houses of the revelations of Allah and wisdom. Lo! Allah is Subtile, Aware

33:35.ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ وَٱلۡمُسۡلِمَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ وَٱلۡقَٰنِتِينَ وَٱلۡقَٰنِتَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ وَٱلصَّٰدِقَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ وَٱلصَّٰبِرَٰتِ وَٱلۡخَٰشِعِينَ وَٱلۡخَٰشِعَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقِينَ وَٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمِينَ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمَٰتِ وَٱلۡحَٰفِظِينَ فُرُوجَهُمۡ وَٱلۡحَٰفِظَٰتِ وَٱلذَّٰكِرِينَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا وَٱلذَّٰكِرَٰتِ أَعَدَّ ٱللَّهُ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣰ وَأَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
33:35.en: Lo! men who surrender unto Allah, and women who surrender, and men who believe and women who believe, and men who obey and women who obey, and men who speak the truth and women who speak the truth, and men who persevere (in righteousness) and women who persevere, and men who are humble and women who are humble, and men who give alms and women who give alms, and men who fast and women who fast, and men who guard their modesty and women who guard (their modesty), and men who remember Allah much and women who remember - Allah hath prepared for them forgiveness and a vast reward

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

33:37.ar: وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِي فِي نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَىٰهُۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَطَرࣰ ا زَوَّجۡنَٰكَهَا لِكَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجࣱ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِ أَدۡعِيَآئِهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡهُنَّ وَطَرࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا
33:37.en: And when thou saidst unto him on whom Allah hath conferred favour and thou hast conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear Allah. And thou didst hide in thy mind that which Allah was to bring to light, and thou didst fear mankind whereas Allah hath a better right that thou shouldst fear Him. So when Zeyd had performed that necessary formality (of divorce) from her, We gave her unto thee in marriage, so that (henceforth) there may be no sin for believers in respect of wives of their adopted sons, when the latter have performed the necessary formality (of release) from them. The commandment of Allah must be fulfilled

33:38.ar: مَّا كَانَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲ فِيمَا فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥۖ سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ فِي ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلُۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ قَدَرࣰ ا مَّقۡدُورًا
33:38.en: There is no reproach for the Prophet in that which Allah maketh his due. That was Allah's way with those who passed away of old - and the commandment of Allah is certain destiny

hXJUgv8mng0.title: Surat Al-Ahzab Summary, Part 1
hXJUgv8mng0.one_line: Al-Ahzab opens the surahs on submission: obeying Allah when the command is uncomfortable, the circumstances are dangerous, or the matter is deeply personal.
hXJUgv8mng0.summary: He places Al-Ahzab at the head of the sixth group of surahs, running to Az-Zumar, all about obedience and full surrender to Allah. Submission sounds simple, he says, but handing over one's life, wealth and preferences entirely is hard, and Al-Ahzab tests it under the hardest conditions: military, social, economic and personal. The opening four commands (taqwa, refusing to follow disbelievers and hypocrites, following revelation whole, and relying on Allah) are the formula for an obedient life. He then walks through the uncomfortable rulings: ending the Arab practice of giving adopted children one's own name, and making the Prophet's wives mothers of the believers, which gave women standing to teach and give rulings. The covenant taken from the prophets means everyone who claims truthfulness will be questioned about it. The Battle of the Confederates shows believers whose hearts reached their throats yet held firm, while hypocrites made excuses, and in that very moment Allah names the Prophet as the model. Inside the Prophet's own home, the wives are offered a choice between worldly comfort and Allah, given special commands, and told men and women carry equal responsibility. The story of Zayd and Zaynab, the one time the Prophet felt reluctance, ends with the rule that a believer finds no hardship in what Allah ordains. He asks the audience to obey without carving out exceptions.

outline.heading: Obedience when it is hard
outline.gist: Following Allah's commands is a deeper and more delicate subject than we assume, and obeying in difficult times is what saves individuals and communities.

outline.heading: The sixth group of surahs: submission from Al-Ahzab to Az-Zumar
outline.gist: Each surah in the group looks at surrender from a different angle; Al-Ahzab takes the angle of obedience under military, social, economic and personal strain.

outline.heading: Adoption and the child's true name
outline.gist: Children are called by their own fathers' names; the Arabs had used adoption to swell their tribes, and the change was uncomfortable for them.

outline.heading: The Prophet's wives as mothers of the believers
outline.gist: The status gave the wives religious, social and political protection and an upper hand among people.

outline.heading: Four opening commands that define an obedient life
outline.gist: Taqwa, not obeying disbelievers and hypocrites, following revelation word for word without exceptions, and relying on Allah while doing so.

HgqjnS2N0VM.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Qalam, Part 2: Verses 8-16
HgqjnS2N0VM.one_line: The ten traits the Prophet was told not to emulate in 68:8-16, and how flipping them gives his character.
HgqjnS2N0VM.summary: After recalling that the juz is about dawah, where victory means people entering the deen rather than conquering land, he reads verses 8-16 as a list of ten traits the Prophet is told not to emulate. He first explains why the Quran often teaches by prohibition: a red line leaves wide space to act, as the shahadah itself begins with a negation. The first trait, the denier who rejects evidence he finds convincing, takes most of the session. Muslims follow evidence, build iman on the universe, history and human experience rather than on reasons for each ruling, and then trust Allah's commands the way a patient trusts a qualified doctor. Religion cannot be inherited, and a good Muslim admits error, as a Syrian Quran scholar did publicly after twenty years and as Abu Bakr did with Umar. He then covers compromise of principle (with a sharp critique of politicians' silence on Gaza), lying and lack of integrity, gossip and talebearing (he refuses to hear any), stinginess, harming others, base conduct, harshness and shame of one's own identity. Flipping all ten yields the Prophet's portrait, which the audience is asked to aspire to.

outline.heading: Recap: dawah as the goal, victory as people entering the deen
outline.gist: Last week's verse set the Prophet upon great character. The juz is about dawah, and An-Nasr defines victory as people entering Allah's religion in crowds, not conquering land, owning things or one empire beating another.

outline.heading: Our causes are about injustice, not ownership
outline.gist: Muslims keep causes central because injustice occurred and the deen requires them to stay a voice of truth; the four opening surahs give the knowledge, ethical, spiritual and behavioural requirements.

outline.heading: Let the outcomes judge whose path is right
outline.gist: Allah knows who is guided, so Muslims need not fight over it: live your values and let the results decide. Fail to live them and people will think Islam failed.

outline.heading: Do not emulate: why the Quran teaches by prohibition
outline.gist: 'La tuti'' here means do not emulate, not only do not obey. A command restricts you to a few options while a prohibition draws a red line and leaves wide space, as in the hadith to avoid what he forbids and do what he commands as much as you can.

outline.heading: The shahadah begins with a negation
outline.gist: Tawhid is stated as 'there is no god' before 'but Allah', which is why it is weighty; he tells atheists they are already halfway there.

outline.heading: Number one: the denier who rejects what he finds convincing
outline.gist: Takdhib is not plain disbelief but saying no to what makes the most sense because of arrogance, envy, fear or a lost interest, and the Quran treats it as a grave sin.

outline.heading: Muslims follow the evidence wherever it leads
outline.gist: As in 'if the Most Merciful had a son I would be the first to worship', Muslims accept truth from anyone, even people they dislike, and are never asked to walk blindly or lie to themselves.

outline.heading: Establish iman by evidence, then trust the commands
outline.gist: Certainty in Allah, the prophethood and the Quran comes through evidence; after that clear commands are followed without a reason for each, the way a patient trusts a qualified doctor without needing a medical degree.

outline.heading: Iman is built on the universe, not on the reasons for rulings
outline.gist: A clever arguer might win a debate over why something is haram, and that changes nothing. Iman is built on the universe, history and human experience, not on why there are five prayers or the Prophet's marriages; a hadith he cannot explain does not shake it.

outline.heading: You inherit your race, not your religion
outline.gist: We are Muslim because Islam makes the most sense, not because we took it from our parents; everyone must study the evidence for a Creator, his communication and his messengers themselves.

outline.heading: Converts lose nothing: Islam returns them to their own prophets
outline.gist: Islam sees other faiths as once led by great men with a book from Allah and later corrupted, so a convert gains the authentic teaching of his own prophet and belongs to his people more.

outline.heading: Stop demanding a reason for every detail
outline.gist: Children learning maths and patients questioning every drug show the flaw: trust the maxims you verified and accept what follows, or go back and fix your iman at its root.

outline.heading: A Syrian Quran master admits twenty years of error
outline.gist: A leading Syrian Quran teacher of his generation defended a disputed tajweed point, a slight lip opening in the hidden mim, for twenty years, then publicly said he had been wrong; Allah raised his name after it.

outline.heading: A challenge should send you back to your own argument
outline.gist: Defending something because it is familiar or ours is not Islamic. A challenge need not change your mind on the spot but should send you to study your own argument, as Muslims hope a Christian will re-examine the Trinity.

outline.heading: Islam never asks you to switch off your brain
outline.gist: Faith built on evidence needs logic; do not take anything on trust from anyone, even family, and write down what spouses owe each other rather than relying on trust.

outline.heading: Not because of our forefathers: Islam has the superior argument
outline.gist: Quraysh asked whether he was better than his grandfather; following forefathers is no argument. We are Muslim because Islam holds the superior argument, not the reverse, so never force things to fit.

outline.heading: The first value: adherence to the truth, and the count-and-flip method
outline.gist: He will count the traits and flip each one, since the mirror image is the Prophet. The first is adherence to truth and evidence without ego, which is why he was chosen and why those like him succeeded around him.

outline.heading: Umar and the woman who corrected him from the minbar
outline.gist: Umar, known for stopping at the Book of Allah, said a woman calling out from the back was right and he was wrong, because her point seemed stronger in that moment, even though his view held on reflection.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr rushes to admit he was wrong
outline.gist: After a quarrel with Umar, Abu Bakr came running to say the fault was his; the Prophet defended him as the one who believed in him when no one else did.

outline.heading: The first prohibition the early Muslims heard
outline.gist: These were among the first commands ever revealed, so the first thing the Quran forbade was being someone biased who will not follow the evidence.

outline.heading: Number two: they wish you would compromise
outline.gist: Idhan is giving something up for a gain. Quraysh, though stronger, kept offering deals, even asking him to seat the slaves behind the nobles, and he conceded nothing, so the stories make him sound like the one with the upper hand.

outline.heading: Politicians stand for nothing: the silence on Gaza
outline.gist: Politicians say anything for a vote, and a man like Trump is sold as a practising Christian. They stay silent on the Holy Land while children are pulled from rubble because they fear Zionist pressure and Muslims have not built enough pressure.

outline.heading: The most principled should lead; instead we pick the lesser evil
outline.gist: The leader should be the most principled person in a group, as the Prophet was. Today voters settle for the least harmful candidate, the Middle East has open dictatorship and the West a hidden one with the illusion of choice.

outline.heading: Number three: the habitual swearer, a liar for gain
outline.gist: Hallaf is a figure of speech for the liar who swears and exaggerates to escape trouble or get something out of people.

outline.heading: Number four: mahin, the one without integrity
outline.gist: Mahin has no sense of his own dignity or word and will flatter anyone or change colour to get his way.

outline.heading: Number five: the slanderer who carries tales
outline.gist: Hammaz mashsha' bi namim carries words between people to make them hate one another; tales you cannot verify only ruin relationships, so namimah is among the worst social sins.

outline.heading: His own rule: refuse to hear any gossip
outline.gist: From early in his marriage he refused all gossip, even about himself. Become boring to gossips and they stop; backbiting is eating a dead brother's flesh.

outline.heading: Rise above it: people will always talk
outline.gist: Drop gossiping friends even if it leaves you alone for a while. No one throws stones at a dead tree; those who talk about you are often envious and later seek your friendship.

outline.heading: Who has time to watch other people's lives?
outline.gist: Commenting on how others dress and behave is not the conduct of focused, purposeful people; he would buy that spare time for an eighth day of the week.

outline.heading: Number six: withholding good
outline.gist: Manna' lil-khayr withholds a kind word, money, time or help again and again, out of a selfishness that wants others to get less so he stays ahead.

outline.heading: Number seven: transgressing against others
outline.gist: Once you harm someone's space, wealth, freedom or integrity only Allah can help you; you cannot remove the pain or return stolen time, and an apology is only a first step. Arrive on the Day with clean hands.

outline.heading: Number eight: athim, conduct the community sees as low
outline.gist: Athim is one who engages in behaviour the community regards as base and unethical, below high character.

outline.heading: Number nine: 'utull, the harsh whom people abandon
outline.gist: 'Utull is the heavy, rude person others leave feeling worse; Allah told the Prophet that had he been harsh even the companions would have scattered, so family and community will not stay with someone who yells.

outline.heading: Number ten: zanim, ashamed of his own identity
outline.gist: Zanim claims a lineage, family or identity that is not his because he is ashamed of his own.

outline.heading: Count the ten, flip them, and you get Muhammad
outline.gist: The opposites are adherence to truth, steadfast principle, honesty, integrity, reconciling people, generosity, gentleness, high character, ease with people and pride in one's identity, which is exactly who the Prophet was.

outline.heading: Wealth, children and the brand on the snout
outline.gist: The one who calls the signs ancient fables because he has wealth and sons will be marked on the nose for all to see.

outline.gist: After the first revelation the Prophet was taken to Waraqah, who explained his whole mission; his name means paper, a seventh reference to knowledge, and the next surah revealed is named the Pen.

outline.heading: Writing is how things sink in: the Libyan memorizers
outline.gist: Typing does not stick but writing does; Libyan and Somali students memorize the Quran by writing it and win the big competitions, and concepts sink in the same way.

outline.heading: Structure a sentence to build a value
outline.gist: He asks people to stop the reels and journal: a word like honesty is abstract until you define it in a sentence, and structuring that sentence is half the work of building an ethic.

outline.heading: The Quran preserved because it was written
outline.gist: Over a thousand companions memorized it, but it reaches us down to every articulation because it was written from day one, on bones, wood and palm leaves when writing material was hard to find.

outline.heading: Defining honesty: a worked example
outline.gist: A notebook will not ruin the Amazon. Honesty means telling the truth when it is uncomfortable or costly, without being rude or blunt about people's feelings.

outline.heading: Values are written: the pens have been lifted
outline.gist: The pen symbolises that values are documented and fixed, as the Prophet said of decree that the pens are lifted and the pages dry.

outline.heading: Fiqh is dynamic, values are fixed
outline.gist: Rulings respond to time, place, person and circumstance, so a new Muslim's fiqh differs from a lifelong Muslim's; honesty, trust, loyalty, kindness and empathy are the same in any century.

outline.heading: Take rulings locally; differ on fiqh, never on values
outline.gist: This surah has almost no fiqh. Ask your local scholar rather than a sheikh in another country; scholars differ on wiping over socks by design, but no sheikh differs on honesty or justice.

outline.heading: A surah every Muslim needs
outline.gist: If he had to choose one surah for people to hear, it would be this one: its values speak equally to the imam, the lifelong Muslim and the new Muslim.

outline.heading: Nun: its recitation and the challenge theory
outline.gist: Nun takes six counts. The most accepted view of the opening letters is that they challenged the Arab poets with their own letters.

outline.heading: The opening letters as coding: a fourth dimension
outline.gist: Surahs sharing the same opening letters share a common thread. Beyond when a surah was revealed, where it sits, and what it does for you, the letters add a fourth dimension we do not yet fully grasp.

outline.heading: Allah's oaths carry content and need an answer
outline.gist: Allah never swears aimlessly: what he swears by tells a story before the answer comes, unlike our oaths by Allah or the Prophet's oath by the One in whose hand is his soul.

outline.heading: The oath by the pen: you are writing your own book
outline.gist: Every choice writes the novel you will read aloud before Allah, perhaps with others listening, with your motives and thoughts laid bare, so choose the story you want to read.

outline.heading: Documentation let humanity build on itself
outline.gist: Written history is scarce until the last millennium or so; once knowledge was recorded, people could absorb a whole civilization's rise and fall in hours and build on it.

outline.heading: Muslims led the boom of documentation
outline.gist: Muslims translated and extended Greek, Persian and Roman learning, Aristotle included, instead of burning it. Writing preserved the Quran exactly and saved the hadith, and narrators who lost their written records were not relied on.

outline.heading: Two readings of 'you are not mad'
outline.gist: The answer to the oath: either by your Lord's grace you are not mad, or, as he prefers, in spreading your Lord's blessing, the Quran, you are not mad.

outline.heading: Called mad, never a liar: forty years without a lie
outline.gist: Madness was the first accusation because Quraysh could not call him a liar after forty years in which no one close to him heard a lie, a rare thing that takes a certain personality.

outline.heading: Ghayr mamnun: a reward never spoiled by reminders
outline.gist: A gift repeatedly brought up becomes a burden, as the Quran warns against spoiling charity with reminders; the reward is free of being told you did not deserve it.

outline.heading: Allah makes you feel you earned it
outline.gist: The Quran attends to the psychological side of reward: whoever enters Paradise knowing it is Allah's bounty is made to feel he earned it, so the joy is complete, which one-word translations like 'unending' miss.

outline.heading: Values and ethics: the ethic is the value made visible
outline.gist: The answer to the oath has three parts, the third being 'upon great character'. A value such as empathy is one word; the ethic is how it shows up with each person, though some philosophers split them as individual versus community.

outline.heading: 'Ala: ethics as the ground you stand on
outline.gist: The Arabs pictured ethics as a foundation you stand upon, letting you hold your head high, see further and not lose your footing.

outline.heading: Chosen for his character; people are like minerals
outline.gist: He had great character before prophethood, and that is why he was chosen. The best of people before Islam are the best in Islam once they learn it.

outline.heading: Umar and Hamza: late converts who excelled through their values
outline.gist: Umar came six years late yet became central to the religion, and the seerah books give his and Hamza's conversions their own chapter, because their values were ready; those who lied and cheated take far longer to change.

outline.heading: Character, not ritual, defines your Islam
outline.gist: People who pray in the first row can still cheat in business. No one in the Quran is praised for ethics like the Prophet, so he is set as the role model to watch and learn from.

outline.heading: Maftun: the trial that shakes your foundation
outline.gist: 'You will see and they will see which of you is tried': a fitnah from Allah is a heavy trial that shakes who you are and can make you lose your footing.

outline.heading: Time exposes values, so don't worry about those who wrong you
outline.gist: The Quran declines to argue and lets time show. Anyone who cheats or mistreats you will have the reputation they deserve before they leave this earth; if they are good it was a slip Allah forgives.

outline.heading: You can't hide patterns forever: the thief's 'first time'
outline.gist: A thief who swore it was his first theft was told Allah never exposes someone at the first slip. This is for your own self-check, not for judging those who are exposed.

outline.heading: Your Lord knows best who strayed: let time show it
outline.gist: The Quran does not argue with the disbelievers; it states the Prophet's character and lets time judge, and fourteen centuries later people still try to emulate him.

outline.heading: Remembered for values, not possessions
outline.gist: Abu Jahl and Abu Lahab are remembered only for opposing him. No one remembers your house or degrees; your values are what remain and testify for or against you.

EC9O6DzHJqU.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Third Article, Reforming Social Values (Part 2)
EC9O6DzHJqU.one_line: Every society has values: reinforce the good ones, push back on the bad, keep this distinct from dawah, and see how the Prophet reformed Arab values.
EC9O6DzHJqU.summary: His second khutbah on the third article of the Aqabah pledge, the Prophet's condition that Madinah accept a reform of its social values. He grounds the article in 'urf, custom, which jurists use as a secondary source of evidence, and in the word ma'ruf, the known good. Every society has values; Muslims should neither pretend otherwise nor try to erase them, but identify what they share, reinforce it in practice, and push back against the rest. He separates this from dawah: calling someone to Islam needs preparation, a relationship and finesse aimed at making them love Allah, while asking someone not to take a handicap spot needs only conviction, and mixing the two loses both. Al-Hajj 22:41 pairs ritual with reformed values. Values abandoned through silence are lost, which he says the confusion around gender shows, and Muslims, Arabs especially, are themselves known for rudeness and disregard for others. The Prophet kept the Arabs' generosity and loyalty but ended racism, female infanticide, usury and autocracy, beginning by consulting people himself. In the second khutbah he cites the warning that abandoning enjoining good brings punishment and unanswered dua, and laments the crime, abuse and dishonesty he sees in the community.

outline.heading: Opening
Returning to the third article: the status quo will not be accepted
outline.gist: Muslims misunderstand this concept and mix it with other things. The Prophet made it a condition of coming to Madinah: some values he would strengthen, explain and praise, others he would push against and remove; he was not coming to validate all of their values.

outline.heading: 'Urf: custom as a source of evidence
outline.gist: Beyond the four agreed sources, Quran, Sunnah, consensus and analogy, scholars use other sources when those are silent, and custom is one of them. The word ma'ruf literally means simply "that which is known".

outline.heading: Ma'ruf: the known good
outline.gist: Being an optimistic desert people, the Arabs used the bare word to mean what is known to be good and beneficial. So ma'ruf is about the norms of your society: the values you agree with you reinforce through behaviour, practice and reminders, and the ones you do not you push back against.

outline.heading: Every society has values
outline.gist: It is arrogant to imagine any people has no values: some write them into a constitution, others simply live them and you notice them over time. Muslims do not ask anyone to erase everything they have and take a new set.

outline.heading: Values work is not dawah
outline.gist: Rituals and acts of worship matter, but bringing people to them is dawah, which has its own art. The distinction exists because once you mix the two, one or both get lost.

outline.heading: Inviting to Islam versus asking him not to block a driveway
outline.gist: Calling a non-Muslim to Islam and asking the same man not to take a handicap spot or block a driveway are different acts done by different people. Not everyone is qualified for dawah: it needs preparation, education, a relationship, the right circumstances and finesse.

outline.heading: The goal of dawah is that they love Allah
outline.gist: The art of dawah is bringing people closer to Allah so they love Him. If you do not know how to do that, be a facilitator and bring someone who does; everyone has a role, but not necessarily the speaking role.

outline.heading: Values need only conviction
outline.gist: Upholding values needs no finesse or preparation: reinforce the ones we share, call out those who break them, and push back on the rest vocally, through advocacy, politics and the media. Both are fully required in the deen, and dawah is the fourth article.

outline.heading: Ritual and values together
outline.gist: In Al-Hajj 22:41 those given authority in the land establish prayer and zakat and command good and forbid wrong: both must happen. Luqman's advice to his son makes everyone responsible for values, though not everyone should be giving religious advice.

outline.heading: Fewer fatwas, more basic decency
outline.gist: Stop passing on a shaykh's opinion as the only one when it is one among many acceptable views. Values are clear: respect, empathy, equality, kindness, standing in line, leaving your car where it blocks no one, the basics of human decency.

outline.heading: Stop fighting for a value and you lose it
outline.gist: In one area of life the basics are already gone: people fear being fired over pronouns and no longer know how to define male and female or who may marry. Stop pointing things out and you lose them, so say plainly that no one may speak to or treat a child, a wife, a client or any human being that way.

outline.heading: Etiquette is itself a value
outline.gist: This is not a call to aggression: speaking to people in the best way is one of our values. Instead Muslims, Arabs especially, are known as rough and loud and as not respecting other people's space.

outline.heading: 'Me first, let the flood take everyone'
outline.gist: The attitude that only my getting through matters is not Islamic. Children must not grow up thinking they can bully others or answer elders disrespectfully; dawah and values overlap, but the Prophet and the Quran distinguished them.

outline.heading: Values are shared by humanity
outline.gist: No one needs to be Muslim to agree that people are equal and deserve the same rights and respect, which is why this is not dawah. When people lose their values they lose everything; the Arabs were generous and kept their word but were deeply racist.

outline.heading: What the Prophet ended
outline.gist: Racism, worse then than in today's worst gatherings, burying newborn daughters, a distorted view of women and usury were values he declared done with. Governance was another: everyone was to have a voice.

outline.heading: Ending one-man rule, starting with himself
outline.gist: Arabs sat before their chief and flattered him; no one's opinion mattered. The Prophet, who had revelation, began asking people what to do, because the Quran told him to consult them, and the change of value started with himself.

outline.heading: Our task: name the values and practise them first
outline.gist: Muslims in this country must identify the values here that are Islamic, be first to practise and teach them, and push back on the rest vocally, appropriately and with sound arguments. It is complicated, and only small silos of Muslims are thinking about it.

outline.heading: Those who clung to the old values lost their status
outline.gist: The Ansar understood that things would change: anyone who kept up tribal hostility, usury or drinking lost his standing. Here our basic values are threatened, and we must acknowledge it before we can change our reality.

outline.heading: Interlude
After Badr: wealth with a right for others
outline.gist: A change of value beyond zakat: wealth that comes in is not only for those who took part but strengthens the poor. The companions disliked it and said what they should not have, revelation told them not to quarrel over it, and they later admitted their conduct.

outline.heading: Command good, or your dua goes unanswered
outline.gist: In an authentic narration the Prophet swore that you will command good and forbid wrong, or Allah will soon send a punishment and then not answer you when you call on Him. Once values rot, what is the point?

outline.heading: White clothes, black heart: the dusty traveller
outline.gist: Praying in the first row dressed in white means nothing if the heart is black. The dishevelled traveller raises his hands to Allah while his food and drink are haram; values decide whether you touch haram when you are hungry or in need.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr corrects the reading of 5:105
outline.gist: Refusing haram in a financial pinch while fearing for your children is a value. Abu Bakr on the minbar told people they recite "you are responsible for yourselves" without understanding it, for he heard the Prophet say that if they do not command good and forbid wrong, Allah will punish them all.

outline.heading: Our community's failing values
outline.gist: Our basic values are being questioned and we are not upholding them: in his work with people he sees crime, domestic abuse, corners cut, untrustworthy dealings and disregard for law and order.

outline.heading: How can we ask for victory?
outline.gist: We keep asking Allah for success and victory while we cannot uphold basic decency, respect or empathy among ourselves. It has changed many times before and will change through people who care, but pretending all is well leaves our children questioning their values.

outline.heading: Outro

31:5.en: Such have guidance from their Lord. Such are the successful

31:6.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشۡتَرِي لَهۡوَ ٱلۡحَدِيثِ لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲ وَيَتَّخِذَهَا هُزُوًاۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ مُّهِينࣱ‏
31:6.en: And of mankind is he who payeth for mere pastime of discourse, that he may mislead from Allah's way without knowledge, and maketh it the butt of mockery. For such there is a shameful doom

31:7.ar: وَإِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ ءَايَٰتُنَا وَلَّىٰ مُسۡتَكۡبِرࣰ ا كَأَن لَّمۡ يَسۡمَعۡهَا كَأَنَّ فِيٓ أُذُنَيۡهِ وَقۡرࣰ اۖ فَبَشِّرۡهُ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
31:7.en: And when Our revelations are recited unto him he turneth away in pride as if he heard them not, as if there were a deafness in his ears. So give him tidings of a painful doom

31:8.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتُ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
31:8.en: Lo! those who believe and do good works, for them are the gardens of delight

31:9.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۖ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣰّ اۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
31:9.en: Wherein they will abide. It is a promise of Allah in truth. He is the Mighty, the Wise

31:10.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ عَمَدࣲ تَرَوۡنَهَاۖ وَأَلۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَوَٰسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمۡ وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَآبَّةࣲۚ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجࣲ كَرِيمٍ
31:10.en: He hath created the heavens without supports that ye can see, and hath cast into the earth firm hills, so that it quake not with you; and He hath dispersed therein all kinds of beasts. And We send down water from the sky and We cause (plants) of every goodly kind to grow therein

31:11.ar: هَٰذَا خَلۡقُ ٱللَّهِ فَأَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦۚ بَلِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
31:11.en: This is the Creation of Allah. Now show me that which those (ye worship) beside Him have created. Nay, but the wrong-doers are in error manifest

31:12.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا لُقۡمَٰنَ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ أَنِ ٱشۡكُرۡ لِلَّهِۚ وَمَن يَشۡكُرۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدࣱ‏
31:12.en: And verily We gave Luqman wisdom, saying: Give thanks unto Allah; and whosoever giveth thanks, he giveth thanks for (the good of) his soul. And whosoever refuseth - Lo! Allah is Absolute, Owner of Praise

31:13.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ لُقۡمَٰنُ لِٱبۡنِهِۦ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُۥ يَٰبُنَيَّ لَا تُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّ ٱلشِّرۡكَ لَظُلۡمٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
31:13.en: And (remember) when Luqman said unto his son, when he was exhorting him: O my dear son! Ascribe no partners unto Allah. Lo! to ascribe partners (unto Him) is a tremendous wrong

31:14.ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ حَمَلَتۡهُ أُمُّهُۥ وَهۡنًا عَلَىٰ وَهۡنࣲ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ فِي عَامَيۡنِ أَنِ ٱشۡكُرۡ لِي وَلِوَٰلِدَيۡكَ إِلَيَّ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
31:14.en: And We have enjoined upon man concerning his partners - His mother beareth him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years - Give thanks unto Me and unto thy parents. Unto Me is the journeying

31:15.ar: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشۡرِكَ بِي مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَاۖ وَصَاحِبۡهُمَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَعۡرُوفࣰ اۖ وَٱتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ مَنۡ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّۚ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
31:15.en: But if they strive with thee to make thee ascribe unto Me as partner that of which thou hast no knowledge, then obey them not. Consort with them in the world kindly, and follow the path of him who repenteth unto Me. Then unto Me will be your return, and I shall tell you what ye used to do

31:16.ar: يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنَّهَآ إِن تَكُ مِثۡقَالَ حَبَّةࣲ مِّنۡ خَرۡدَلࣲ فَتَكُن فِي صَخۡرَةٍ أَوۡ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ أَوۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَأۡتِ بِهَا ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
31:16.en: O my dear son! Lo! though it be but the weight of a grain of mustard-seed, and though it be in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Lo! Allah is Subtile, Aware

31:17.ar: يَٰبُنَيَّ أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأۡمُرۡ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَٱنۡهَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَصَابَكَۖ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ عَزۡمِ ٱلۡأُمُورِ
31:17.en: O my dear son! Establish worship and enjoin kindness and forbid iniquity, and persevere whatever may befall thee. Lo! that is of the steadfast heart of things

31:18.ar: وَلَا تُصَعِّرۡ خَدَّكَ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَمۡشِ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَرَحًاۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخۡتَالࣲ فَخُورࣲ‏
31:18.en: Turn not thy cheek in scorn toward folk, nor walk with pertness in the land. Lo! Allah loveth not each braggart boaster

31:19.ar: وَٱقۡصِدۡ فِي مَشۡيِكَ وَٱغۡضُضۡ مِن صَوۡتِكَۚ إِنَّ أَنكَرَ ٱلۡأَصۡوَٰتِ لَصَوۡتُ ٱلۡحَمِيرِ
31:19.en: Be modest in thy bearing and subdue thy voice. Lo! the harshest of all voices is the voice of the ass

31:20.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَسۡبَغَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعَمَهُۥ ظَٰهِرَةࣰ وَبَاطِنَةࣰۗ وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِي ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲ وَلَا هُدࣰ ى وَلَا كِتَٰبࣲ مُّنِيرࣲ‏
31:20.en: See ye not how Allah hath made serviceable unto you whatsoever is in the skies and whatsoever is in the earth and hath loaded you with His favours both without and within? Yet of mankind is he who disputeth concerning Allah, without knowledge or guidance or a scripture giving light

31:21.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَا وَجَدۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ يَدۡعُوهُمۡ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
31:21.en: And if it be said unto them: Follow that which Allah hath revealed, they say: Nay, but we follow that wherein we found our fathers. What! Even though the devil were inviting them unto the doom of flame

31:22.ar: ۞وَمَن يُسۡلِمۡ وَجۡهَهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحۡسِنࣱ فَقَدِ ٱسۡتَمۡسَكَ بِٱلۡعُرۡوَةِ ٱلۡوُثۡقَىٰۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡأُمُورِ
31:22.en: Whosoever surrendereth his purpose to Allah while doing good, he verily hath grasped the firm hand-hold. Unto Allah belongeth the sequel of all things

31:23.ar: وَمَن كَفَرَ فَلَا يَحۡزُنكَ كُفۡرُهُۥٓۚ إِلَيۡنَا مَرۡجِعُهُمۡ فَنُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
31:23.en: And whosoever disbelieveth, let not his disbelief afflict thee (O Muhammad). Unto Us is their return, and We shall tell them what they did. Lo! Allah is Aware of what is in the breasts (of men)

31:24.ar: نُمَتِّعُهُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا ثُمَّ نَضۡطَرُّهُمۡ إِلَىٰ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظࣲ‏
31:24.en: We give them comfort for a little, and then We drive them to a heavy doom

31:25.ar: وَلَئِن سَأَلۡتَهُم مَّنۡ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ ٱللَّهُۚ قُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِۚ بَلۡ أَكۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
31:25.en: If thou shouldst ask them: Who created the heavens and the earth? they would answer: Allah. Say: Praise be to Allah! But most of them know not

31:26.ar: لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ
31:26.en: Unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth. Lo! Allah, He is the Absolute, the Owner of Praise

31:27.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقۡلَٰمࣱ وَٱلۡبَحۡرُ يَمُدُّهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ سَبۡعَةُ أَبۡحُرࣲ مَّا نَفِدَتۡ كَلِمَٰتُ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
31:27.en: And if all the trees in the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas to help it, (were ink), the words of Allah could not be exhausted. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Wise

31:28.ar: مَّا خَلۡقُكُمۡ وَلَا بَعۡثُكُمۡ إِلَّا كَنَفۡسࣲ وَٰحِدَةٍۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ
31:28.en: Your creation and your raising (from the dead) are only as (the creation and the raising of) a single soul. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

31:29.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِي ٱلَّيۡلِ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ كُلࣱّ يَجۡرِيٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ى وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
31:29.en: Hast thou not seen how Allah causeth the night to pass into the day and causeth the day to pass into the night, and hath subdued the sun and the moon (to do their work), each running unto an appointed term; and that Allah is Informed of what ye do

31:30.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ
31:30.en: That (is so) because Allah, He is the True, and that which they invoke beside Him is the False, and because Allah, He is the Sublime, the Great

31:31.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ تَجۡرِي فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِنِعۡمَتِ ٱللَّهِ لِيُرِيَكُم مِّنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارࣲ شَكُورࣲ‏
31:31.en: Hast thou not seen how the ships glide on the sea by Allah's grace, that He may show you of His wonders? Lo! therein indeed are portents for every steadfast, grateful (heart)

31:32.ar: وَإِذَا غَشِيَهُم مَّوۡجࣱ كَٱلظُّلَلِ دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّىٰهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡبَرِّ فَمِنۡهُم مُّقۡتَصِدࣱۚ وَمَا يَجۡحَدُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارࣲ كَفُورࣲ‏
31:32.en: And if a wave enshroudeth them like awnings, they cry unto Allah, making their faith pure for Him only. But when He bringeth them safe to land, some of them compromise. None denieth Our signs save every traitor ingrate

31:33.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡاْ يَوۡمࣰ ا لَّا يَجۡزِي وَالِدٌ عَن وَلَدِهِۦ وَلَا مَوۡلُودٌ هُوَ جَازٍ عَن وَالِدِهِۦ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّۖ فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡغَرُورُ
31:33.en: O mankind! Keep your duty to your Lord and fear a Day when the parent will not be able to avail the child in aught, nor the child to avail the parent. Lo! Allah's promise is the very truth. Let not the life of the world beguile you, nor let the deceiver beguile you, in regard to Allah

31:34.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُۥ عِلۡمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ ٱلۡغَيۡثَ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِي نَفۡسࣱ مَّاذَا تَكۡسِبُ غَدࣰ اۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِي نَفۡسُۢ بِأَيِّ أَرۡضࣲ تَمُوتُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرُۢ
31:34.en: Lo! Allah! With Him is knowledge of the Hour. He sendeth down the rain, and knoweth that which is in the wombs. No soul knoweth what it will earn to-morrow, and no soul knoweth in what land it will die. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

ajidMJIHuAI.title: Surat Luqman Summary
ajidMJIHuAI.one_line: Surat Luqman as a guide to relationships between generations, built on wisdom: how parents raise children and how children treat parents.
ajidMJIHuAI.summary: He places Luqman in the cluster from al-Qasas to as-Sajdah about our relationships: with others' stories, with trials, with Allah's laws in the universe, and here between generations. Luqman is one of only two non-prophets with a surah named after them, honoured because he was an educator of generations, and education requires wisdom. The surah opens with those who buy idle talk, which he links to the recklessness of youth and also to preachers who lack wisdom, raising unimportant religious topics that make young people lose interest or mock the deen. Duty to parents continues even if they push you away from Islam: you do not obey them in that, but you remain the best companion to them. From Luqman's advice he draws a method for parents: speak tenderly; introduce your child to Allah first; ask for one core ritual, prayer, rather than overloading them; encourage social participation in good; teach patience at home before the world tests them; teach humility and manners with vivid images and humour, as with the donkey's voice. He warns that following forefathers is not always right: parents may not use birr to dictate a child's university or residence, and children must not follow harmful traditions. Wisdom, knowledge joined to experience, is endless like Allah's words.

outline.heading: A cluster of surahs about relationships
outline.gist: Relationships are among the most important aspects of human life.

outline.heading: Relationships with stories, trials, cosmic laws and generations
outline.gist: The earlier surahs treat our relationship with others' stories, with calamities and with Allah's laws; Luqman turns to generations.

outline.heading: Recap of al-Qasas, al-Ankabut and ar-Rum
outline.gist: Each surah of the group addresses one relationship in our surroundings.

outline.heading: Why a surah is named after Luqman
outline.gist: Apart from Maryam he is the only non-prophet so honoured, because he was an educator of generations.

outline.heading: Education requires wisdom: the book of wisdom
outline.gist: The surah opens by pointing to wisdom.

outline.heading: Idle talk and the recklessness of youth
outline.gist: Lack of wisdom leads to wasted talk and mockery of serious matters, including careless talk about religion.

outline.heading: Idle talk that leads away from Allah's path
outline.gist: Young people by nature waste time in talk that brings no benefit and distances them from Allah.

outline.heading: Unwise preaching turns youth away
outline.gist: Choosing unimportant religious topics, or the wrong time and way, makes the next generation lose interest and mock even valid teachings.

outline.heading: Luqman's wisdom, gratitude and duty to parents
outline.gist: The mother's burden, and remaining their best companion even if they push you away from Islam.

outline.heading: Good companionship with parents even when you cannot obey
outline.gist: Knowing our duties to those above and below us holds society together.

outline.heading: Advice given tenderly: do not associate partners
outline.gist: Wa'z means advising with kindness and gentleness.

outline.heading: The mustard seed: Allah is subtle and aware
outline.gist: Nothing escapes Allah, wherever it is hidden.

outline.heading: Prayer, enjoining good, and patience
outline.gist: Commanding good and forbidding wrong as participation in social reform; life brings misfortunes that require perseverance.

outline.heading: Do not turn your cheek or strut; be moderate
outline.gist: Visual images help young people grasp the lesson.

outline.heading: The donkey's voice: humour to reach a child
outline.gist: Luqman likely used humour to relate to his son; advice begins with tenderness.

outline.heading: Introduce children to Allah first; one ritual is enough
outline.gist: Ask for prayer at this age rather than overloading children with rituals.

outline.heading: Social participation and patience learned at home
outline.gist: Push children to take part in good, and teach patience before the first calamity outside the home overwhelms them.

apeX4BUhbFU.title: Surah Summaries: Al-Zalzalah and Al-Adiyat
apeX4BUhbFU.one_line: Al-Zalzalah: Earth testifies against her children and judgment rests on simple good and evil; Al-Adiyat: the horse's loyalty shames human disloyalty to Allah.
apeX4BUhbFU.summary: He frames the final surahs as small concentrated doses of Islamic values. Al-Zalzalah, he says, is a single snapshot of the Day of Judgment: the earth, the one constant every human leans on and the mother of all people equally, convulses, expels the dead and then tells her stories. She reports what her children did to one another and also what they did to her, the polluted rivers, the felled trees, the ruined air. Hearing a harsh truth from someone so close is what leaves people walking dazed. Judgment then rests on an atom's weight of good and evil, measured by an innate moral sense that every human has before religion confirms it. Were you a force of goodness, of evil, or a mixture? Al-Adiyat carries one idea, loyalty. Its oaths paint a short film of panting horses striking sparks and charging into an army at dawn with no hesitation, though their owner gave them only food and water. The human, given far more by Allah, is kanud, a word joining disloyalty and ingratitude. We stay loyal only while life goes our way, and like Ibn Rawahah at Mu'tah even a moment's hesitation costs rank. He asks the audience to stop asking for more and start giving back their time, empathy, expertise and wealth.

outline.heading: The short surahs as concentrated pills of Islamic values
outline.gist: Each final surah condenses what longer surahs explain at length, so knowing them gives a person the core values needed to reach Allah.

outline.heading: Both surahs early Makkan; Al-Zalzalah is about judgment
outline.gist: Both were revealed early in Makkah. Al-Zalzalah teaches accountability and specifically what judgment will be based on.

outline.heading: The Quran shows the Last Day in snapshots
outline.gist: No single passage narrates the whole Day of Judgment; each surah gives a snapshot, and this one is the earth's testimony on which judgment rests.

outline.heading: The earth convulses and throws out her burdens
outline.gist: The great quake expels everyone from their graves. Earth is the one constant we lean on, and every human, of every race, is equally her child.

outline.heading: What is wrong with her? When the constant breaks
outline.gist: Earth has always sheltered and fed us; when she breaks the norm, nothing is certain anymore, and that is what shocks the human being.

outline.heading: She tells her stories: how her children treated each other
outline.gist: Earth witnessed every deed done in private, and she will report the killing, oppression and cruelty, all of which grieve a mother whoever is fighting.

outline.heading: She also tells what we did to her
outline.gist: She will complain of polluted rivers, cut trees and ruined air: her children were unkind to one another and to their own mother.

outline.heading: People emerge scattered, hurt by the harsh truth
outline.gist: A harsh truth from someone very close wounds deeply and is never forgotten; hearing every truth about our greed and extravagance leaves people walking aimlessly.

outline.heading: An atom's weight: judgment by simple good and evil
outline.gist: Earth does not care about sectarian and theological divisions. Humans know good and evil innately; religion confirms it and gives it intention.

outline.heading: Earth's final testimony before she passes
outline.gist: Having served humanity for billions of years, earth gives her last testimony; who judges children better than their mother? Were you a force of good, evil or both?

outline.heading: Al-Adiyat: a linguistic masterpiece on loyalty
outline.gist: The surah carries one thought only, loyalty, and expresses it in breathtaking language.

outline.heading: The oaths as a short film: panting chargers striking sparks
outline.gist: The oaths draw a picture of horses galloping so hard their breathing is audible and their hooves strike sparks from rock; he takes a question on whether horses or camels are meant and says it makes little difference.

outline.heading: The dawn raid: dust raised and straight into the army
outline.gist: They attack at dawn, raise a storm of dust and charge fearlessly into the middle of an enemy host.

outline.heading: What did you ever give the horse?
outline.gist: Its owner gave it only food, water and a pat, yet it never hesitates or questions being ridden toward death. Its loyalty is complete.

outline.heading: Kanud: disloyal and ungrateful in one word
outline.gist: The human being is kanud toward his Lord, the one word in Arabic that joins disloyalty with ingratitude. Allah has given us far more than we ever gave an animal.

outline.heading: Loyal only while things go our way
outline.gist: One curve ball and we question everything despite years of blessings. A rider cannot work with a horse that hesitates; Allah says trust me and keep going.

outline.heading: Mu'tah: the cost of a second's hesitation
outline.gist: Zayd and Ja'far held the banner until death; Abdullah ibn Rawahah hesitated for a moment before fighting, and the Prophet described his rank as slightly below theirs.

outline.heading: We always want a little more
outline.gist: Picture a horse asking for one more day of food before it rides out; that is how humans bargain with Allah.

outline.heading: The 93-year-old who wanted two more years
outline.gist: A terminally ill elderly patient kept hoping for two more years and then two more. Wanting more is human, but it must not block loyalty to Allah.

outline.heading: What Allah asks back: time, empathy, expertise, wealth
outline.gist: Most will not be asked for their lives, but Allah asks for time, attention, empathy, knowledge and wealth; will we give or keep asking for more?

outline.heading: The graves overturned and the hidden exposed
outline.gist: Everything hidden in graves and in hearts is brought out; every hesitation, doubt and disloyalty will be clear to the Lord who knows all.
